building.name: Long Beach Building Code: the California Building Code (Title 24, Part 2), adopted by Long Beach Municipal Code section 18.40.010 with local amendments in Chapter 18.40
building.effective: 2026-01-01 (Ordinance ORD-25-0019, which restates Title 18 in its entirety; City Council public hearing 2025-10-21)
building.quote: 18.40.010 – Adoption of California Building Code. The City Council adopts and incorporates by reference as though set forth in full in this chapter the 2025 Edition of the California Building Code ... The following sections, chapters or appendices of the California Building Code are deleted: Sections 101 through 116 of Chapter 1, Division II, Section 3113 of Chapter 31, and Section 3308 of Chapter 33; Chapters 27, 28, 29, 31A, 31C, 31D, 31E, 31F, 32, and 34; and Appendices A, B, C, D, E, F, H, J, K, L, M, N, and O. ... Such codes and code provisions shall constitute and be known as the Long Beach Building Code.

other_quotes.quote: Effective January 1, 2026, all projects must comply with the 2025 Edition of the California Building Standards Code and the Long Beach Municipal Code (LBMC) to receive approval from the Long Beach Community Development Department, as required by State law.

ORDINANCE NO. ORD-25-0019 AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LONG BEACH AMENDING THE LONG BEACH MUNICIPAL CODE BY AMENDING AND RESTATING TITLE 18 IN ITS ENTIRETY, AND ADOPTING LOCAL AMENDMENTS TO THE 2025 EDITION OF THE CALIFORNIA BUILDING STANDARDS CODES AND THE 1997 EDITION OF THE UNIFORM HOUSING CODE, ALL OF WHICH ARE KNOWN AS THE LONG BEACH BUILDING STANDARDS CODE ... it shall take effect on the thirty-first (31st) day after it is approved by the Mayor, but in no event prior to January 1, 2026.

The City of Long Beach is conducting a public hearing to adopt and amend the 2025 Edition of the California Building Standards Code ... The proposed changes will go into effect on January 1, 2026. ... Meeting Date: October 21, 2025

building.note: The city's amendments to the building code (sections 18.40.020 to 18.40.830) cover definitions, occupancy classification, fire sprinklers, standpipes and alarms, exits, efficiency dwelling units, flood design, seismic and structural design, wood framing, pool enclosures and flood appendix G. None touches toilet rooms, toilet compartments, interior finishes or accessibility (Chapter 11B). The city deletes the state code's administrative sections (Chapter 1, Division II, sections 101 to 116) and uses its own in LBMC Chapters 18.01 to 18.10, so permit exemptions are the city's (LBMC 18.04.020), not state section 105.2. It also deletes Chapter 29 (Plumbing Systems), which in California only points to the plumbing code. The signed copy's date of final passage was not readable in the PDF text (the draft is dated 10/21/2025).

plumbing.name: Long Beach Plumbing Code: the California Plumbing Code (Title 24, Part 5), adopted by Long Beach Municipal Code section 18.43.010
plumbing.quote: 18.43.010 – Adoption of California Plumbing Code. The City Council adopts and incorporates by reference as though set forth in full in this chapter the 2025 Edition of the California Plumbing Code ... The following appendices of the California Plumbing Code are included: Appendices A, B, D, G, H, I, and R. The following sections, chapters, or appendices of the California Plumbing Code are deleted: Sections 101.0 through 107.2 and Table 104.5 of Chapter 1, Division II; Chapters 13, 15 and 16; and Appendices C, E, F, J, K, L, M, N, O, P, Q, and S.
plumbing.note: Chapter 18.43 has this one section only. The city deletes the plumbing code's administrative sections, three chapters (13, 15, 16) and some appendices, and changes no technical section. Chapter 4 (fixtures, section 422 and Table 422.1) is adopted unchanged.

fixtures.text: Long Beach adopts the 2025 California Plumbing Code in one section (LBMC 18.43.010) and makes no technical amendment to it, so section 422 and Table 422.1 apply as the state wrote them and the state pack's worked examples stand. No Building and Safety information bulletin on fixture counts exists in the city's bulletin list (IB-057, plumbing plan submittals, and IB-015, tenant improvements, say nothing about counts).
fixtures.quote: The adoption of the California Plumbing Code is subject to the changes, amendments and modifications to said code as provided in this chapter [Chapter 18.43 contains only section 18.43.010]
fixtures.worked_examples_note: Not redone: the table is the state's. The statements used in the page text (50/50 split, urinals, women's count, single restroom for 50 or fewer, new buildings, additions and changes of use, floor area per person) come from the 2025 California Plumbing Code as read for the California pack, not from a Long Beach document.

permit.rule_quote: 18.04.010 – Permits required. A. Building permits. No person, firm or corporation shall erect, construct, enlarge, alter, repair, remodel, move, remove, improve, convert or demolish any building or part of a building or structure, or change the character or occupancy or use of any building or structure, or part of a building or structure, in the City without first obtaining a permit covering such work from the Building Official.

permit.partitions_note: The list names 'partitions' only as nonfixed and movable ones not over 5 feet 9 inches high, and as temporary exhibit partitions. It does not name toilet partitions or say whether floor-anchored or overhead-braced toilet compartments count as nonfixed and movable. page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Long Beach job sites. Price your restroom in five questions and see the California and city rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Long Beach port and logistics buildings, hotels, schools and medical offices, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Long Beach uses California's rules, which set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Long Beach requires a building permit to alter, repair or remodel any part of a building unless the work is on its exempt list. The list covers work valued at $1,000 or less, unless it affects fire safety, the structure or a required accessible route, and "nonfixed and movable" partitions up to 5 feet 9 inches high. It doesn't name toilet partitions, so ask the Building and Safety Bureau (562-570-7648) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the Long Beach Building and Safety Bureau
page.stalls_intro: Long Beach counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women, and California's rules require urinals in the men's room. Every toilet needs a stall, and urinals need screens between them. The women's room must have at least as many toilets as the men's room has toilets and urinals together.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for new buildings, additions and changes of use that bring in more people. An office or shop with 50 people or fewer may have a single one-person restroom. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, California's plumbing rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, and a restaurant dining room or a classroom at one per 30 square feet. Your architect or the Long Beach Building and Safety Bureau sets the final number.
page.install_rule: Long Beach issues building permits to a contractor who holds a valid California contractor license and an active Long Beach business license, and asks for proof of workers' compensation insurance if the contractor has employees. California requires its contractor license, usually the C-61/D-34 class, for partition installs of $1,000 or more, and at any price when the job needs workers or a permit. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: In Long Beach the contractor needs a California contractor license for jobs of $1,000 or more, and a Long Beach business license to take out a permit.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** California requires the state-set wage on public jobs over $1,000, including city and school district work. For a carpenter on building work in Los Angeles County that is $54.41 an hour plus $29.91 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 11% in Long Beach: 7.25% statewide, 3% in Los Angeles County district taxes and 0.75% city. The city's budget says its share returns to 1% on October 1, 2027.
page.buyers_extra: - **Port, terminal and waterfront buildings:** solid plastic (HDPE) or phenolic with stainless steel hardware, for restrooms that see hard use and damp air.

page.official_names: - The rules by their official names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; California Building Code Chapter 11B; Long Beach Building Code (the 2025 California Building Code with City of Long Beach amendments, Long Beach Municipal Code Chapter 18.40, in force since January 1, 2026); Long Beach Plumbing Code (the 2025 California Plumbing Code, Long Beach Municipal Code Chapter 18.43, same date); NFPA 286 for HDPE under the International Building Code, the model for California's code.
notes: To confirm by phone before launch: whether a like-for-like toilet partition replacement in an existing commercial restroom needs a Long Beach building permit (Building and Safety Bureau, 562-570-7648).
Long Beach's $1,000 exemption does not cover work that affects a required accessible route; the code doesn't say whether replacing the partitions of an accessible stall counts.
The city's "Do I Need A Permit?" web page shows an older version of the exempt list than the restated Title 18 (ORD-25-0019); the page text follows the ordinance.

City permits are not required for buildings owned or controlled by the federal government, the State, Los Angeles County or a public school district, and work in the Harbor District needs the Board of Harbor Commissioners' permission first; the page text leaves both out.
The Long Beach Municipal Code library (Municode) blocks automated access: check in a browser that the city has no ordinance of its own on single-user or all-gender restrooms.
The link in research/local-rules/cities.json for Long Beach (longbeach.gov/lbds/building/building-regulations) returns 404; the rule itself is confirmed on the city's Building Permits page.

The statements on the 50-person single restroom, the floor area per person and the counts applying to new buildings, additions and changes of use come from the state plumbing code as read for the California pack, not from a Long Beach document.
Sales tax: recheck the CDTFA rates page before October 1, 2027, when the city's budget says the city share returns to 1% (the total would then be 11.25%).
